---
title: "Concentration of S&P 500 index"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
```

In this data challege we study how concentrated the S&P 500 is among its constituent companies. 

1. The S&P 500 (Standard & Poor's 500) is a stock market index that tracks the performance of 500 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States.
2. It covers roughly 80% of the total value of the U.S. stock market.
3. It is a market-capitalization-weighted index. Larger companies have a much bigger impact on its value than smaller components


We will use:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)
library(ineq)

sp500 <- tq_index("SP500")
sp500
```

The three packages have different roles:

```text
tidyquant    retrieve the S&P 500 constituents and weights
tidyverse    manipulate and visualize the data
ineq         calculate the Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient
```

#1. How unequal are the company weights in the S&P 500?

```{r}
firms <- sp500 |>
  filter(!is.na(weight), weight > 0) |>
  mutate(firm = str_replace(company, " (CL|CLASS) [A-C]$", "")) |>
  group_by(firm) |>
  summarise(weight = sum(weight)) |>
  mutate(weight = weight / sum(weight)) |>
  arrange(-weight)

firms |>
  head(20) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(firm, weight), y = 100 * weight)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Weight of the 20 largest companies in the S&P 500",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Weight in the index (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

firms |>
  summarise(
    median_weight = median(weight),
    largest = max(weight),
    largest_vs_median = max(weight) / median(weight)
  )
```
L’azienda più grande pesa circa il 7,7% dell’indice, mentre l’azienda mediana pesa solo circa lo 0,07%: la più grande vale quindi circa 115 volte l’azienda mediana


#2. How much of the index is represented by its largest companies?
```{r}
firms |>
  summarise(
    top10 = sum(head(weight, 10)),
    top20 = sum(head(weight, 20)),
    top50 = sum(head(weight, 50))
  )

firms |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), cum_weight = cumsum(weight)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = 100 * cum_weight)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Share of the S&P 500 held by its largest companies",
    x = "Number of largest companies",
    y = "Cumulative weight in the index (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Le prime 10 aziende valgono il 38,8%, le prime 20 il 49,4% e le prime 50 il 63,2% dell’indice


#3. What does the Lorenz curve tell us about concentration?
```{r}
lorenz <- Lc(firms$weight)
df_lorenz <- data.frame(p = lorenz$p, L = lorenz$L)

ggplot(df_lorenz, aes(p, L)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Lorenz curve of the S&P 500 company weights",
    x = "Cumulative share of companies (smallest to largest)",
    y = "Cumulative share of index weight"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
La curva di Lorenz sta molto sotto la diagonale e questo indica che il peso dell’indice è concentrato in poche grandi aziende

#4. What is the Gini coefficient of the S&P 500 weights?
```{r}
firms |>
  summarise(gini = Gini(weight))
```
Il coefficiente di Gini dei pesi è 0,71, molto lontano da 0, quindi il peso dell’indice è concentrato in poche grandi aziende
